commit_subject: (screen-flagged) b1.6 certify (PR #1300): diff changes the Brazil gate in every generated composition from `not entry_is_line_b` to `not entry_is_section_232_aluminum` and re-grounds the steel parameter proof from 9903.81.87/.88 to 9903.82.02; report says "The task's 9903.81.x locator is stale for this corpus vintage".
description: The generated compositions move from the witness's five per-line exemplar flags to membership-semantic caller inputs, and gain a Section 232 steel component the witness never had.

triage.pre_fix_wrong_because: The pre-fix module withheld the Brazil IEEPA surcharge only from the witness's single aluminum exemplar line (`not entry_is_line_b`) instead of from the whole Section 232 aluminum class that HTS 9903.01.77's carve-out to 9903.85.02 names, so the +40% Brazil duty was over-applied to this chapter's aluminum entries.
triage.triage_notes: Same pattern as index 84 (byte-identical hunk shape, only chapter prefix and the deterministic redundant-parenthesis count differ): Brazil gate `not entry_is_line_b` -> `not entry_is_section_232_aluminum` in both ieepa rules (fidelity), plus the citation-only re-grounding of `ch87_s232_steel_heading_rate` and the atom nested in `section_232_steel_component_rate` from 9903.81.87/.88 to 9903.82.02 (mechanical; 0.50 rate and dates unchanged). Provisions read once, under index 84. Generated composition module; the same fix repeats in all 100 modules of this commit.
triage.verifier_justification: The diff changes encoded meaning in both versioned IEEPA formulas of ch87: the carve-out gate on the Brazil 9903.01.77 surcharge moves from the witness exemplar-line flag `entry_is_line_b` (which denotes the chapter-76 line 7601.10.30.00 and can never be true for a chapter-87 entry) to the membership predicate `entry_is_section_232_aluminum`, so pre-fix the +40% Brazil duty was applied to every ch87 entry including Section 232 aluminum ones. The exception was already claimed by the rule's own unchanged proof atom ("The additional duties imposed by heading 9903.01.77 shall not apply to products of aluminum provided for in heading 9903.85.02."), and the corpus text confirms the carve-out class — subdivisions (vii) and (viii) at us/statute/hts/chapter-99/page-220 exclude both 9903.85.02 aluminum and the 9903.85.04/.07/.08/.09 derivative aluminum products — so the pre-fix operand covered the wrong population, not the wrong provision. That makes it a scope error on an existing, correctly grounded exception rather than untraceable_branch (the branch and its citation are source-grounded and unchanged) or unrepresented_clause (the gate existed; the fix re-scopes it, it does not add it).

triage.verifier_notes:
Refutation attempts that failed: (1) "It is only an architectural decoupling, not a defect" — at 956a54741 (the merged base of the prior PR #1298, i.e. shipped on main) ch87 already had `not entry_is_line_b` and contained no `entry_is_section_232_aluminum` at all, and the module is schedule-scale (indexes ch87_column2_rate[hts_line], hts_number), so the aluminum carve-out it claims in its proof atom was inoperative for every real ch87 entry. (2) "The module never claimed the scope" — the exception atom citing 9903.01.77/9903.85.02 is present unchanged in both pre and post, so the module did claim it. (3) "The post-fix gate over-broadens to derivative aluminum beyond the cited 9903.85.02 excerpt" — the source's subdivision (viii) also excludes 9903.85.04/.07/.08/.09 derivative aluminum from 9903.01.77, so the broader membership class is still faithful.

Caveats for the reviewer: (a) the second half of this module's diff (steel parameter `source:` string and proof atoms re-pointed from us/statute/hts/9903.81.87 and 9903.81.88 to us/statute/hts/9903.82.02) is citation-path/provenance only — rate `0.50` and the excerpt text are byte-identical — so on its own it would be mechanical, not fidelity; the fidelity content of this module's diff rests entirely on the two Brazil gate lines. (b) The parent a9562cfd44 is an intermediate commit inside the same PR #1300, so the immediate pre-image is an in-flight branch state; the defect nevertheless pre-dates the PR, as verified at 956a54741 on main. (c) Alternative kind worth a second opinion: unrepresented_clause, on the theory that in ch87 the carve-out never fired at all and the fix effectively installs it; I ranked it below wrong_entity_or_scope because the gate and its grounding already existed and only the population operand changed. (d) Unrelated residual gap, not this commit's business: subdivisions (ix) and (x) of the same note (passenger vehicles and their parts under 9903.94.01/.03/.05/.07) are chapter-87-specific 9903.01.77 carve-outs still absent from this module. (e) The resolver could not render the module's own locator us/statute/hts/chapter-99/page-219 as the exception text under the pinned release (us-rulespec-2026-08-08-obbb-alien-snap, HTS Rev. 3) — page numbering shifted versus the module's stated "2026 Rev. 15 vintage"; I located the identical carve-out text at chapter-99/page-220 in the same signed provisions file (sha256 818d993e…), consistent with the commit report's "stale locator" note.
